candidates.statement: In general, FDA’s guidance documents do not establish legally enforceable responsibilities. 37 Instead, guidances describe the Agency’s current thinking on a topic and should be viewed only 38 as recommendations, unless specific regulatory or statutory requirements are cited. candidates.statement: Sponsors should consider the following regarding structural endpoints for developing medical 46 products for the treatment of OA: 47
candidates.context: II. CONSIDERATIONS FOR DEVELOPMENT 44 • FDA recognizes that OA can be a serious disease with an unmet medical need for 49 therapies that modify the underlying pathophysiology of the disease and potentially 50 change its natural course to prevent long-term disability. However, there are several 51 ongoing issues with developing such products, including the multifactorial and complex 52 etiopathogenesis of the disease, the well-recognized discordance between structural 53 changes and signs/symptoms/function, the lack of standard definitions of disease 54 progression, and, correspondingly, the absence of endpoints to reliably assess the ability 55 of a product to alter OA disease progression. 56

candidates.statement: • To accept structural endpoints as valid outcome measures for accelerated approval, there 65 should be substantial confidence, either based on empirical evidence from randomized, 66 controlled comparisons from clinical trials and/or based on a comprehensive 67 understanding of the disease process and product mechanism of action, that an effect on 68 the candidate structural endpoint will reliably predict an effect on the clinical outcomes 69 of interest. 5 The ultimate goal of treatments related to inhibition of structural damage or 70 targeting the underlying pathophysiology associated with OA is to avoid or significantly 71 delay the complications of joint failure and the need for joint replacement, and also to 72 reduce the deterioration of function and worsening of pain. 73
candidates.context: • Because of the complex and variable pathologic changes through which OA impairs 58 function and leads to long-term disability and/or joint replacement, at this time it is 59 unclear what magnitude of change in structural endpoints would translate to a clinically 60 meaningful benefit to patients (i.e., reliably predict both reduced pain and increased 61 function or prolonged time to end-stage disease). Thus, no structural endpoints have 62 been used for traditional or accelerated approval in OA to date. 63 4 We update guidances periodically.
